newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens upbeat on profit expectations.
newsitem.headline: Siemens upbeat on profit expectations.

text.p: Karl-Hermann Baumann, chief finance officer of Siemens AG, said on Monday the electronics group expected above average growth in profits for the next few years.

"For the time being we are maintaining our profit forecast in the range of 2.5 billion marks after taxes," he said, commenting on the year that ends on September 30 in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.

He said Siemens "saw certain improvement in income before taxes" but expected its tax liablility to increase. For this year, Siemens would achieve a 10 percent return on equity. It aimed to reach a 15 percent return by the year 2000.
For 1998/99, Siemens expected "a healthy increase in sales and a rise in profit," he said.
Baumann also said he expected Siemens Nixdorf Informationssystem (SNI), the company's computer division, to nearly double profits to over 100 million marks in 1996/97 from 52 million marks last year.
He also said the communications division profit was currently above expectations.
